newsitem.title: UK: ScotAm outlines members payouts in Pru deal.
newsitem.headline: ScotAm outlines members payouts in Pru deal.

text.p: Scottish Amicable on Thursday published details of the proposed transfer of business to Prudential Corp and benefits to policyholders in the wake of the mutual insurer's acquistion in March.
A policyholder circular outlining the plans will be mailed to members over the next week.
The plans have to be approved by voting members at a special general meeting to be held on June 27 and confirm proposals made during the bid.
The Pru beat off rival offers from Abbey National and Australian Mutual Provident (AMP) to win control of ScotAm and reinforce its position as Britain's number one fund manager.
ScotAm chairman Sandy Stewart said the bidding process had produced a high value for the business and a full distribution of the assets in the with-profits fund to with-profits policyholders.

"The members of ScotAm now have the opportunity to vote for a package which will provide additional financial security and the prospect of improved future investment returns leading to enhanced payouts," said Stewart.
Around 1.1 million qualifying members will share 600 million pounds ($981.7 million) in compensation for loss of membership rights in the Pru deal.
All will receive a fixed cash payment of 250 pounds with a variable amount based on the bonuses added to with-profits policies at December 31 1996.

A special bonus worth 470 million pounds will go to with-profits policies and 530 million pounds representing the estimated current value of further bonuses will be added to with-profits policies as they pay-out.
The Pru is to inject 1.3 billion pounds of financial support to enable increased investment freedom for the ScotAm with profits fund, enhancing the potential for better returns.
ScotAm policies are to be transferred to the Pru and held in a dedicated fund, serviced from ScotAm's Stirling headquarters.
